source.excerpt:
\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{l >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X}
\toprule
\textbf{Architectural Dimension} & \textbf{Classical Symbolic MAS} & \textbf{Generative LLM Agents} \\
\midrule
\textbf{Cognitive Substrate} & Modal logic, first-order rules, unification & Dense multi-layer neural networks ($\sim 10^{11}$ params) \\
\textbf{Goal Representation} & Explicit syntactic desires and intention stacks & Latent prompt conditioning and reward steering \\
\textbf{Commitment Dynamics} & Formal axioms (blind, single-minded, open) & Soft stochastic retention; vulnerable to context drift \\
\textbf{Concurrency Control} & Message passing, rendezvous, Petri nets & Ad-hoc prompt warnings (``do not edit simultaneously'') \\
\textbf{Failure Handling} & Explicit recovery goals (e.g., $-!g$ in AgentSpeak) & Probabilistic backtracking or hallucinated apologies \\
\textbf{Security \& Boundaries} & Formal capability tokens, deontic permissions & System prompts easily bypassed via indirect injection \\
\textbf{Physical Mutex} & Database locks, OS semaphores & None; relies entirely on host process environment \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\caption{Comparative analysis of Classical Symbolic MAS versus Generative Neural Agents.}
\label{tab:lineage-comparison}
\end{table}

items.title: Table 0.2
items.caption: Canonical commitment strategies in BDI agent architectures.
items.purpose: Canonical commitment strategies in BDI agent architectures.

source.excerpt:
\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{lX}
\toprule
\textbf{Commitment Strategy} & \textbf{Formal Drop Axiom} \\
\midrule
\textbf{Blind (Fanatical)} & Maintains $\mathrm{Int}(\mathbf{A}\lozenge \phi)$ until $\mathrm{Bel}(\phi)$ holds. \\
& $\mathrm{Int}(\mathbf{A}\lozenge \phi) \land \neg\mathrm{Bel}(\phi) \to \mathbf{A}\big(\mathrm{Int}(\mathbf{A}\lozenge \phi) \;\mathcal{U}\; \mathrm{Bel}(\phi)\big)$. \\
& \emph{Pathology:} Induces infinite loops if $\phi$ becomes physically impossible. \\
\addlinespace[3pt]
\textbf{Single-Minded} & Drops $\phi$ if achieved \emph{or} believed impossible. \\
& $\mathrm{Int}(\mathbf{A}\lozenge \phi) \land \neg\mathrm{Bel}(\phi) \land \mathrm{Bel}(\mathbf{E}\lozenge \phi) \to \mathbf{A}\big(\mathrm{Int}(\mathbf{A}\lozenge \phi) \;\mathcal{U}\; (\mathrm{Bel}(\phi) \lor \neg\mathrm{Bel}(\mathbf{E}\lozenge \phi))\big)$. \\
& \emph{Standard:} Balances persistence with dynamic feasibility. \\
\addlinespace[3pt]
\textbf{Open-Minded} & Drops $\phi$ if achieved, impossible, \emph{or no longer desired}. \\
& $\mathrm{Int}(\mathbf{A}\lozenge \phi) \land \dots \land \mathrm{Des}(\mathbf{A}\lozenge \phi) \to \mathbf{A}\big(\mathrm{Int}(\mathbf{A}\lozenge \phi) \;\mathcal{U}\; (\mathrm{Bel}(\phi) \lor \neg\mathrm{Bel}(\mathbf{E}\lozenge \phi) \lor \neg\mathrm{Des}(\mathbf{A}\lozenge \phi))\big)$. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\caption{Canonical commitment strategies in BDI agent architectures.}
\label{tab:commitment-strategies}
\end{table}

\toprule
\textbf{Grade} & \textbf{Meaning} \\
\midrule
\Built & Realized, exercised, and true under the production runtime. \\

\textbf{I1a / I1b} & Durability \emph{split by fault class}: I1a (process-crash) is \Built; I1b (power-loss) is \NotGuar{} under the default WAL configuration. A claim that conflates fault classes cannot carry one grade. \\

\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\caption{The seven subsystems, each the contract the daemon holds for the layer above it,
with the table that is its home where the chapter names one and its maturity grade.
All seven are disciplines over one SQLite/WAL file: one commit history, not seven
stores. The grades come from the chapter's own status table (\S\ref{swk:app:status}).}
\label{swk:tab:swk-seven-organs}
\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.15}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.22\textwidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.19\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Subsystem} & \textbf{Contract held for the layer above} & \textbf{Maturity} \\
\midrule
transactional substrate & one writer, one durable file; every other subsystem is a table with discipline over the same commit history & \Built \\
resource / exclusion & at most one compatible holder per conflict domain; leases expire and are swept lazily (home: \texttt{claims}) & \Built \\
actor continuity & a stable actor identity across sessions, mechanically present but asserted by the actor, not proven & \BuiltWeak\ self-asserted \\
message carriage & an ordered, cursor-addressable, durable envelope delivered at least once (home: \texttt{messages}) & \Built \\
obligation \& enforcement & no \emph{done} without a receipt the daemon can re-check; the policy monitor detects and cannot always prevent (home: \texttt{commitments}) & \BuiltWeak\ partial \\
session memory & notes and events survive process death; execution state does not & \Built\ (memory) \\
self-attestation & the daemon reports its own coverage as enforced, degraded or stubbed, never silently & \Built \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

% Brief (tikz-diagram-craft).
% Reader question: how much evidence does each downstream link actually
%   inherit from the one before it?
% Claim: support drops at the first hop (memory to checkpoint: full to notes
%   only) and drops again at the second (continuity to the outcome ledger:
%   notes only to partial); identity and market can never exceed that
%   partial residue, because downstream confidence cannot exceed the
%   weakest upstream link.
% Evidence: whitepaper/single-writer-kernel.tex sec:continuity, the memory
%   (Built) / checkpoint (BuiltWeak, notes not execution state) / outcome
%   ledger (BuiltWeak, commitments and oracle-bound closure, not neutral
%   graded outcomes) status classification.
% Must distinguish: the two drops, and that identity/market are capped at
%   the outcome ledger's own level, not independently graded.
% Grammar: computed step plot in pd axis, direct labels, the worked drops
%   dropped to their ticks (S11). Rejected: a bare status table (Built /
%   BuiltWeak per organ), which states the grade but not that it composes
%   downstream as a maximum.
% Five-second test: "a staircase down at hop one, flat, down again at hop
%   two, then flat to the end".
\begin{figure}[H]
\centering
\pdfigurehue{pdcobalt}%
\begin{tikzpicture}[pd figure]
\begin{axis}[pd axis,
  width=8.6cm,
  height=5.0cm,
  axis lines=left,
  symbolic x coords={memory,checkpoint,continuity,outcome,identity,market},
  xtick=data,
  xticklabels={memory,check\\point,continuity,outcome\\ledger,identity,market},
  xticklabel style={align=center,text width=1.55cm,pd label},
  ytick={0,1,2,3},
  yticklabels={none,partial,{notes only},full},
  ymin=-.3,ymax=3.6,
  enlarge x limits=0.09,
  ylabel={evidence the next link can inherit},
  clip=false,
]
\addplot[pd focus series,const plot,mark=*] coordinates
  {(memory,3) (checkpoint,2) (continuity,2) (outcome,1) (identity,1) (market,1)};
\coordinate (cp) at (axis cs:checkpoint,2);
\coordinate (oc) at (axis cs:outcome,1);
\end{axis}
\draw[pd guide] (cp) -- ++(0,1.55cm);
\node[pd label,anchor=south,text width=2.9cm,align=center] at ($(cp)+(0,1.65cm)$)
  {recovery restores notes, not execution state};
\draw[pd guide] (oc) -- ++(0,1.55cm);
\node[pd label,anchor=south,text width=2.9cm,align=center] at ($(oc)+(0,1.65cm)$)
  {outcomes witnessed only in part};
\end{tikzpicture}
\caption{The continuity chain as an evidence-support profile, computed from
the chapter's own status grades. What checkpoint inherits from memory
already drops from full to notes only; what the outcome ledger inherits from
continuity drops again, to partial; identity and market inherit only that
partial residue, not an independent grade of their own. Downstream
confidence cannot exceed the weakest upstream link. [internal]}
\label{fig:swk-continuity-organs}
\end{figure}

% Brief (tikz-diagram-craft). Register row ch1-32 [should].
% Reader question: what does replay actually restore, and what does it
%   explicitly not restore?
% Claim: event-sourced rehydration restores the durable half -- a commit,
%   a message log, open claims and commitments -- by replaying inputs into
%   a fresh agent; it does not and cannot restore the model's inference
%   state, which is bound to a particular model, sampler and session.
% Evidence: whitepaper/single-writer-kernel.tex sec:continuity (Event-
%   sourced rehydration, Designed): pin the working tree to the
%   predecessor's commit, truncate the durable message log to the recorded
%   failure point, replay into a fresh agent; "a replayed prefix
%   reconstructs the inputs to that state, not the state."
% Must distinguish: durable inputs (restored) from inference state (not
%   restored, and named as the open half of OP-4); that this is a
%   direction with an unestablished completeness claim, not a closure.
% Grammar: a four-step pipeline with a dashed exclusion box around what is
%   not restored (S8: remove one element and the claim survives -- here
%   the exclusion box IS the claim, so it stays). Rejected: a before/after
%   pair, which would need two full agent states drawn and would suggest
%   the "after" is a faithful restoration rather than a reconstruction of
%   inputs only.
% Five-second test: "four boxes in a row; a dashed box below the last one
%   says what never comes back".
\begin{figure}[H]
\centering
\pdfigurehue{pdcobalt}%

\toprule
\textbf{\#} & \textbf{Invariant (theorem)} & \textbf{Mechanism} & \textbf{Maturity} \\
\midrule
I1a & Process-crash durability & WAL + OS page cache & \Built \\
I1b & Power-loss durability & (needs full synchronization) & \NotGuar \\
I2 & Mutual exclusion (1 holder/key) & uniqueness constraint + busy-wait & \Built \\
I3 & Idempotence of re-claim/re-release & upsert / delete-if-exists & \Built \\
I4 & Liveness reclamation (TTL sweep) & lazy expiry on read + ticks & \Built \\
I5 & Metric-control separation (Law 1) & daemon-derived deadline & \Built \\
I6 & Oracle-bound closure (Law 2) & finite oracle vocabulary & \Built \\

source.excerpt:
\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\caption{The substrate-layer threat model. The same-user adversary is \emph{out of
scope} by design; several ``security'' subsystems become necessary only against the
cross-machine adversary, which belongs to the economy layer.}
\label{swk:tab:threat-model}
\small
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.23\textwidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.27\textwidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Adversary} & \textbf{In/out of scope} & \textbf{What defends (or does not)} \\
\midrule
Buggy cooperating agent & \textbf{in} & Claims, commitments, post-commit monitoring, oracle-bound closure. The primary design target. \\
Misbehaving agent (ignores advisory claims) & partial & Edit-surface claims are \emph{advisory coordination}, not OS-enforced isolation. A malicious agent can write the file anyway (no kernel-level sandbox such as Landlock, \texttt{unveil}, or Seatbelt). \\
Same-user process (reads/edits the DB) & \textbf{out} & The database is owner-read/write only; OS-keychain isolation of the signing key remains incomplete. Hash-chain tamper-evidence defends against \emph{nobody} under this exclusion (\S\ref{swk:sec:merkle}). \\
Different-uid process & \textbf{in (partial)} & Owner-only permissions on the database and both socket files; but the socket peer-credential check is a software handshake (a self-reported agent identity checked against the registration table), \emph{not} the kernel-enforced socket credential (\texttt{SO\_PEERCRED}) --- a real authentication caveat. This row is the document's operative statement: no other section supersedes it (\S\ref{swk:sec:merkle} specifies hardening that would, but does not ship). \\
Cross-machine / cross-operator & \textbf{out (economy layer)} & Needs the complete local identity contract (\BuiltWeak) and cross-operator attestation (the economy paper). \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

% Brief (tikz-diagram-craft). Register row ch1-44 [could], desert
% Sec. 13.3 "Partial actor-soul identity bounds every other invariant".
% Reader question: which invariants become unsound if identity enforcement
%   stays incomplete?
% Claim: I12 (non-forgeable identity) is a hard precondition for I7, I8 and
%   I9 -- each is only as strong as its least-protected identity path, so a
%   gap in I12 propagates to all three, not just to identity checks.
% Evidence: whitepaper/single-writer-kernel.tex sec:invariants (the
%   invariant table: I7 no-amnesia/note monotonicity, I8 forbidden-state
%   handling, I9 tamper-evidence of the audit log, I12 non-forgeable
%   identity, all \BuiltWeak); the paragraph naming I12 as the hard
%   precondition; Exercise~\ref{ex:swk-forged-release} (a self-asserted
%   identity lets a forged release through because I12 failed to
%   authenticate the input, not because the lock rule was wrong).
% Must distinguish: I12 is the one root, not a peer; the dependency is one
%   direction (I12 bounds the others, not the reverse).
% Grammar: one node fanning out to three (S13: one iconic drawing, no
%   internal mechanism repeated -- I12's own mechanism lives in
%   sec:invariants and is not redrawn here). Rejected: a 2x2 of invariant
%   pairs, which has no natural cell for a one-root, three-dependent claim.
% Five-second test: "one box, three arrows out, one line each on what
%   breaks".
\begin{figure}[H]
\centering
\pdfigurehue{pdcobalt}%
\begin{tikzpicture}[pd figure,x=1cm,y=1cm]
  \node[pd focus state,minimum width=3.0cm,text width=2.6cm,align=center]
    (i12) at (1.55,.75) {I12\\non-forgeable identity};
  \foreach \i/\n/\t/\d in {%
    0/i7/{I7 -- no-amnesia}/{note monotonicity unsound with a forged actor},
    1/i8/{I8 -- forbidden-state handling}/{a forged identity clears a check meant for someone else},
    2/i9/{I9 -- tamper-evidence}/{the audit log names the wrong author}}{
      \node[pd state,minimum width=3.2cm,text width=2.9cm,align=center] (\n) at (7.9,{4.35-\i*3.6}) {\t};
      \draw[pd focus arrow] (i12.east) -- (\n.west);
      \node[pd label,anchor=north,text width=3.8cm,align=center] at (7.9,{3.65-\i*3.6}) {\d};}
\end{tikzpicture}
\caption{I7--I9 depend on authenticated identity at every write path. A legacy path that accepts self-asserted identity can bypass otherwise correct owner checks; I12 remains partial. [internal]}
\label{fig:swk-i12-dependency}
\end{figure}

\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\caption{Open-problem status, stated once. \Closed{} = settled in this chapter;
\Partial{} = something ships but not the property as posed; \Open{} = not solved,
whether or not a design exists. The last column grades the \emph{design}, not the
problem, on the scale of Table~\ref{swk:tab:honestkey}.}
\label{swk:tab:op-status}
\small
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}p{0.09\textwidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.15\textwidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.26\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{\#} & \textbf{Problem} & \textbf{Status} & \textbf{Design in this chapter} \\
\midrule
OP-1 & Fair exclusion without a scheduler & \Open & Stigmergic ticket-lock, \Designed{} (\S\ref{swk:sec:resource}) \\
OP-2 & Regimentation vs.\ enforcement & \Closed & Theorem~\ref{swk:thm:decidability} + Theorem~\ref{swk:thm:regimentation-controllability} \\
OP-3 & Cross-runtime soundness (I11) & \Open & Differential fuzzing, \Designed{} (\S\ref{swk:sec:invariants}) \\
OP-4a & Checkpoint with teeth: durable lineage replay & \Open & Event-sourced rehydration, \Designed{} (\S\ref{swk:sec:continuity}) \\
OP-4b & Checkpoint with teeth: inference-state recovery & \Open & --- \\
OP-5 & Oracle completeness & \Open & State-machine assertions, \Designed{} (\S\ref{swk:sec:enforcement}) \\
OP-6 & Tamper-evidence on the read path & \Open & --- \\
OP-7 & Schema evolution without a sequencer & \Partial & Ordered boot ledger \BuiltWeak; \texttt{user\_version} sequencer \Designed{} (\S\ref{swk:sec:substrate}) \\
OP-8 & Stigmergic decay calibration & \Open & --- \\
OP-9 & Same-machine adversary & \Open & Ephemeral-UID sandbox + kernel-verified peer credential, \Designed{} (\S\ref{swk:sec:merkle}) \\
OP-10 & Per-write-path durability & \Open & Selective checkpointing, \Designed{} (\S\ref{swk:sec:durability}) \\
OP-11 & Cross-subsystem atomicity by default & \Open & One local transaction (\S\ref{swk:sec:atomicity}) --- a buildable defect \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\caption{Mechanism-to-artifact map for the reference implementation. Module names
are illustrative of the organization, not a stable public interface.}
\label{swk:tab:appendix-map}
\small
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Mechanism (body)} & \textbf{Realizing module(s)} & \textbf{Notes} \\
\midrule
Single write connection / pragmas & database-handle module & opens and configures SQLite \\
Port \& lock claims & service-registry, locks, session-files modules & three claim granularities \\
Message bus / tuple space / markers & bus, tuples, marker modules & at-least-once delivery \\
Policy monitor & monitor module & post-commit log subscriber \\
Commitments \& obligation & commitment, obligation-monitor modules & two of the hardening laws shipped \\
Memory \& recovery & session, episodic-memory, recovery modules & recovery passes notes only \\
Audit log \& hash chain & activity-log, hash-chain modules & verification not yet on the read path \\
Self-attestation & attestation, invariant-registry modules & boot gate + pre-flight + watchdog \\
Authorization chain & delegation-chain module & mechanically verified \\
Enforcement gate (macaroon discharge) & kernel macaroon module & crypto verified; in-band, not yet compulsory (\S\ref{swk:sec:enforcement-gap}) \\
Runtime-parity shim & runtime-shim module & normalizes binding differences \\
Identity (actor souls + credentials) & actor-souls, budget-guard modules & bounded gate ships; full write-boundary enforcement absent \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

tableRowsTex: HS256 pinning: the verifier takes the algorithm from policy
the algorithm is never read from the token; later phases change the key type, not who chooses
Ed25519 identity: the daemon signs with a private key, verifiers hold only the public key
no verifier holds a secret that could mint a card; a stolen public key mints nothing
delegation: a child card carries its parent chain, checked as a subset at every hop
the subset check is per hop and monotone, so no later hop widens scope or lifetime
revocation: epoch filters gossiped between daemons and consulted at every acceptance
post-issue authority (a leaked card that should die before its TTL)
acceptance requires the current epoch, so every daemon that holds the epoch refuses the revoked card

% A UML sequence diagram of the issue-delegate-verify ceremony, drawn from the
% chapter's own Phase-3 pseudocode: Daemon.IssueToken (Alg. asymmetric),
% Agent.Delegate and Harbor.VerifyChain (Alg. delegation), with the capability
% sets of Def. offline-attn (["db:read","db:write"] narrowed to ["db:read"]).
%
% Root key: sk_daemon / pk_daemon. Settled from source, not from the prose:
% analyses/harbor_card_v3_delegation.pv, _v5_attenuation.pv,
% _v6_multihop_attack.pv and _v7_multihop_fixed.pv all declare
% `free daemon_sk: skey [private]` and verify the chain root under
% `pk(daemon_sk)`, and core/harbor-card-rs/src/lib.rs binds its verifier to one
% *issuer* public key whose subject is the daemon fingerprint. Alg. delegation
% already requires "Daemon Public Key: pk_daemon"; the chapter's `pk_root` was
% an undeclared alias for that same key and is removed in the same change.
%
% Conventions in force, so that nothing in the drawing varies except what the
% protocol varies: one arrow style for every communication; activation boxes
% on lifelines for "this participant is working"; a reflex self-message for
% the verifier's own loop; arrowheads stopped 0.16cm short of the box they
% address; message labels wrapped to sit inside their own lane, so they need
% no opaque backing and cross no lifeline -- which is why `pd direct label`
% is used here with fill=none throughout.
%
% The readable fact is the shaded region: every message after m1 is inside it,
% and the Daemon's lifeline crosses it carrying no activation box at all.
%
% Per-claim verification, against rendered PDF geometry at 1.0x / 150 dpi under
% BOTH preambles (chapter: anchor-protocol-whitepaper.pdf p.8; Book:
% coordination-papers-mega-volume.pdf p.95). Read off get_drawings(), not by
% eye:
%   - "shaded region": the fill is real ink in both editions, not merely a
%     declared style. Modal grey inside the region against paper outside it
%     separates by 14 levels (5.5%) under the chapter preamble and 34 levels
%     (13.3%) under the Book's, and the region additionally carries a drawn
%     edge. This is the one styling word the caption spends, and it is kept.
%   - "every message after m1 falls inside": the region spans y 359.5..618.9
%     (chapter). m1 is at y 336.8, ABOVE it; m2 421.8, m3 506.9, the verifier's
%     reflex 9.35/10.05 and m4 591.9 all fall within. Same ordering in the Book
%     at y 252.4..511.7. No message label crosses the boundary either.
%   - "where the Daemon is not addressed": the four lifelines are at x 180.5,
%     264.1, 347.8, 431.4 (chapter). Inside the region no arrow endpoint comes
%     within 6pt of x 180.5, and the Daemon carries no activation box below
%     y 359.5 -- its only box is at y 330..345, above the region. The lifeline
%     itself runs the full depth, so the reader sees a participant present and
%     unspoken-to rather than a participant that vanished.
%   - NO dash-bearing path exists in this figure in either edition (zero paths
%     carry a dash array), so there is nothing here for the `pd guide`
%     antialiasing failure to reach. That is deliberate: the earlier version of
%     this figure promised a dotted lifeline that rendered solid, and the fix
%     was to stop encoding the fact in a dash at all.
% [internal; the chapter's own algorithms and the ProVerif models]
\begin{figure}[H]
\centering
\begin{tikzpicture}[pd figure,x=1cm,y=1cm,
  msg/.style={pd direct label,fill=none,align=center,anchor=south,inner ysep=3pt}]

  % ---- the offline region, drawn first so every mark sits on top of it ----
  % Encoded, not annotated: the reader sees a region with a drawn edge, and
  % that edge is itself the divider under message 1.
  \draw[pd neutral fill] (-5.85,-12.55) rectangle (5.00,-3.40);
  % The region's name runs up its own left gutter -- inside the region it
  % names, clear of every lifeline, and not mistakable for a note set loose
  % under the drawing.
  \node[pd note,rotate=90,anchor=south,align=center] at (-5.73,-7.98)
    {offline: the Daemon is not contacted again};

  % ---- participants ----
  \node[pd actor,text width=1.35cm,align=center] at (-4.72,0) {Daemon};
  \node[pd actor,text width=1.35cm,align=center] at (-1.77,0) {Agent A};
  \node[pd actor,text width=1.35cm,align=center] at ( 1.18,0) {Agent B};
  \node[pd actor,text width=1.35cm,align=center] at ( 4.13,0) {Harbor};

  % ---- lifelines: one style for all four. Who is idle is shown by the
  %      absence of an activation box, not by a second line style. ----

\begin{lstlisting}[caption={Algorithm 3: Authorization Chain Verification},label={anchor:alg:delegation}]
Require: Daemon Public Key: pk_daemon
Require: Subset Relation: subseteq on capabilities

function Agent.Delegate(token_parent, sk_parent, agent_child, cap_sub):
    (msg_parent, sigma_parent) <- token_parent
    (_, agent_parent, harbor, cap_parent) <- Decode(msg_parent)
    if cap_sub not_subseteq cap_parent:
        return _|_  // Cannot escalate capabilities
    msg_delegate <- Encode_delegation(msg_parent, sigma_parent, agent_child, cap_sub)
    sigma_delegate <- Ed25519.Sign(msg_delegate, sk_parent)
    emit Delegated(agent_parent, agent_child, cap_sub)
    return (msg_delegate, sigma_delegate)

function Harbor.VerifyChain(chain, pk_daemon):
    tok_root <- chain[0]
    (msg_0, sigma_0) <- tok_root
    if not Ed25519.Verify(msg_0, sigma_0, pk_daemon):
        return _|_  // Invalid root signature
    cap_prev <- ExtractCaps(msg_0)
    pk_current <- pk_daemon
    for i <- 1 to |chain| - 1:
        (msg_i, sigma_i) <- chain[i]
        if not Ed25519.Verify(msg_i, sigma_i, pk_current):
            return _|_  // Invalid delegation signature
        cap_i <- ExtractCaps(msg_i)
        if cap_i not_subseteq cap_prev:
            return _|_  // Per-hop capability escalation detected
        cap_prev <- cap_i
        pk_current <- ExtractPubkey(msg_i)
    emit Accepted(agent_final, harbor, cap_prev)
    return T
\end{lstlisting}

\toprule
\textbf{Threat (\S\ref{anchor:sec:problem})} & \textbf{Closed where} & \textbf{By what mechanism} & \textbf{Residual risk} \\
\midrule
Port squatting (``Ghost in the Harbor'') &
\S\ref{anchor:sec:correct}, Arbiter invariant \texttt{PID\allowbreak\_SQUATTING} &
Cards bind to the connecting process via the daemon's socket-credential check; the Arbiter flags a port claimed by a PID other than its holder &
Detection is post-commit, and the binding is an OS check outside the ProVerif model. See \S\ref{anchor:sec:limitations}, ``A program is not a person'' \\
\addlinespace
Resource contention (shared-state corruption) &
Appendix~\ref{anchor:sec:anchor-limitations-boundaries}; SQLite single-writer &
One writer per harbor, WAL checkpointing, and \texttt{LOCK\_OWNER\_VALID} in the Arbiter &
Enforced by the storage layer, not proved in this chapter; measurable I/O cost \\
\addlinespace
Privilege escalation across delegation &
\S\ref{anchor:sec:delegation}; Property~\ref{anchor:thm:attn-sound} &
Per-hop capability attenuation, checked at issuance and re-checked at verification, mechanized against an insider escalation adversary &
Mechanized at depth~3 and single-hop for the enriched order; depth is a spawn-time policy check, not a verification-time invariant \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

\begin{lstlisting}[caption={\texttt{harbor\_card\_v2\_asymmetric.pv} --- Verified in ProVerif 2.05}]
(* Port Daddy: Harbor Card v2 (Ed25519 / EdDSA) Formal Model *)
type id. type skey. type pkey. type jti. type capability.

free c: channel.
free k_dist: channel [private]. (* Trusted key distribution *)

(*** Digital Signatures (Ed25519) ***)
fun pk(skey): pkey.
fun sign(bitstring, skey): bitstring.
reduc forall m: bitstring, k: skey;
  check_sign(m, pk(k), sign(m, k)) = true.

fun encode_token(id, id, jti, capability): bitstring [data].

(*** Events ***)
event Issued(id, id, jti, capability).
event Accepted(id, id, jti, capability).

(*** Queries ***)
free secret_key: skey [private].
query attacker(secret_key).

query a: id, h: id, j: jti, cap: capability;
  event(Accepted(a, h, j, cap)) ==> event(Issued(a, h, j, cap)).

(*** Processes ***)
let Daemon(a_id: id, h_id: id, j: jti, cap: capability) =
  in(k_dist, sk_h: skey);
  let msg = encode_token(a_id, h_id, j, cap) in
  let signature = sign(msg, sk_h) in
  event Issued(a_id, h_id, j, cap);
  out(c, (msg, signature)).

let Harbor(pk_h: pkey, expected_h: id) =
  in(c, (msg: bitstring, signature: bitstring));
  if check_sign(msg, pk_h, signature) = true then
    let encode_token(a: id, h: id, j_1: jti, cap_1: capability)
      = msg in
    if h = expected_h then
      event Accepted(a, h, j_1, cap_1).

(*** Main Process ***)
process
  new agent_id: id; new harbor_id: id;
  new token_jti: jti; new secret_cap: capability;
  let harbor_pk = pk(secret_key) in
  out(c, harbor_pk);
  (
    (!Daemon(agent_id, harbor_id, token_jti, secret_cap)) |
    (!Harbor(harbor_pk, harbor_id)) |
    (!out(k_dist, secret_key))
  )
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{lstlisting}[caption={\texttt{harbor\_card\_v3\_delegation.pv} --- reflexive-order model (see §\ref{anchor:sec:attn-soundness} for the soundness caveat and the enriched v5 proof)}]
(* Port Daddy: Harbor Card v3 (Delegation Chains) Formal Model *)
type id. type skey. type pkey. type capability.

free c: channel.

(*** Cryptographic Functions ***)
fun pk(skey): pkey.
fun sign(bitstring, skey): bitstring.
reduc forall m: bitstring, k: skey;
  check_sign(m, pk(k), sign(m, k)) = true.

reduc forall c1: capability; is_subset(c1, c1) = true.

fun base_token(id, id, id, capability): bitstring [data].
fun delegate_token(bitstring, id, capability): bitstring [data].

(*** Events ***)
event IssuedRoot(id, id, capability).
event Delegated(id, id, capability).
event Accepted(id, id, capability).

(*** Queries ***)
free harbor_id: id.
query b: id, cap: capability, a: id;
  event(Accepted(b, harbor_id, cap)) ==>
    (event(IssuedRoot(a, harbor_id, cap))
     && event(Delegated(a, b, cap)))
    || event(IssuedRoot(b, harbor_id, cap)).

(*** Processes ***)
free daemon_id: id.
free daemon_sk: skey [private].

let Daemon(a: id, cap: capability) =
  let msg = base_token(daemon_id, a, harbor_id, cap) in
  let s = sign(msg, daemon_sk) in
  event IssuedRoot(a, harbor_id, cap);
  out(c, (msg, s)).

let AgentA(a: id, a_sk: skey, b: id, sub_cap: capability) =
  in(c, (msg: bitstring, s: bitstring));
  let base_token(=daemon_id, =a, =harbor_id,
    root_cap: capability) = msg in
  if check_sign(msg, pk(daemon_sk), s) = true then
    if is_subset(sub_cap, root_cap) = true then
      let d_msg = delegate_token((msg, s), b, sub_cap) in
      let d_s = sign(d_msg, a_sk) in
      event Delegated(a, b, sub_cap);
      out(c, (d_msg, d_s)).

let Harbor(a_pk: pkey) =
  in(c, (d_msg: bitstring, d_s: bitstring));
  let delegate_token((base_msg: bitstring, base_s: bitstring),
    b: id, sub_cap: capability) = d_msg in
  let base_token(=daemon_id, a: id, =harbor_id,
    root_cap: capability) = base_msg in
  if check_sign(base_msg, pk(daemon_sk), base_s) = true then
  if check_sign(d_msg, a_pk, d_s) = true then
  if is_subset(sub_cap, root_cap) = true then
    event Accepted(b, harbor_id, sub_cap).

(*** Main Process ***)
process
  new sk_a: skey;
  let pk_a = pk(sk_a) in
  out(c, pk_a);
  new id_a: id; new id_b: id; new cap_root: capability;
  (
    (!Daemon(id_a, cap_root)) |
    (!AgentA(id_a, sk_a, id_b, cap_root)) |
    (!Harbor(pk_a))
  )
\end{lstlisting}

\begin{lstlisting}[caption={\texttt{harbor\_card\_v5\_attenuation.pv} (excerpt) --- Verified in ProVerif 2.05}]
(* Sound order: reflexive + read <= write; write <= read NOT derivable *)
fun is_subset(capability, capability): bool
reduc
    forall x: capability; is_subset(x, x) = true
    otherwise is_subset(cap_read, cap_write) = true.

(* Insider adversary: holds a real root, signs an over-broad delegation *)
let MaliciousA(a: id, a_sk: skey, b: id) =
  in(c, (msg: bitstring, s: bitstring));
  let base_token(=daemon_id, =a, =harbor_id, root_cap: capability) = msg in
  if check_sign(msg, pk(daemon_sk), s) = true then
    event EscalationAttempted(a, root_cap, cap_write);
    let d_msg = delegate_token((msg, s), b, cap_write) in
    out(c, (d_msg, sign(d_msg, a_sk))).

(* Q1 soundness: a write-card delegated from a read-root is NEVER accepted *)
query b: id; event(Accepted(b, harbor_id, cap_write, cap_read)) ==> false.
(* Q2 non-vacuity: the escalation IS reachable (the proof is not vacuous) *)
query a: id, r: capability, s: capability;
  event(EscalationAttempted(a, r, s)) ==> false.
\end{lstlisting}

% single mechanism.
% Grammar chosen: relation map, three principal nodes in a triangle with

% by one trust-boundary rectangle (the S12 Dolev-Yao convention already

% Fragment: fig-sealed-work-order-schema.tex -- the work order C's
% thirteen fields, grouped by role, as an annotated record schema.
%
% Reader question: what exactly does the one contract both principals
% sign pin down, and what forces a re-sign?
% Claim: the work order's thirteen fields fall into five roles -- pins,
% permissions, recipients, bounds, and remedies -- and changing any one
% field changes the hash, which invalidates both signatures.
% Evidence: "The work order" paragraph, website-v2/public/whitepaper/
% sealed-harbor.tex, Sec. sealed-design (the tuple C, and "Read the tuple
% in order..."; "Any change makes a new hash and requires both
% signatures.").
% Must distinguish: the chapter's own five-way grouping (not a flat list
% of thirteen fields); and, within "pins," that a hash pins the runtime's
% attested MEASUREMENT, not its live state -- the counter-read this
% figure exists to preempt.
% Grammar chosen: block stack (tpl-block-stack), one band per role, the
% record's own field names on the right, a one-line gloss closing each
% band -- fields "sit inside" a role the way a block stack's layers sit
% on each other, and no arrows are needed since containment is the claim.
% Grammar rejected: a flat itemized list of thirteen fields -- loses the
% five-way grouping that is the chapter's own organizing idea and that
% Exercise-level readers are expected to reproduce from memory.
% Five-second test: name the one field that pins the runtime, and say
% what it pins (a measurement, not a live state).
% QA: beauty_lint warns B2 in maritime/technical (row-divider hairlines
% 1.0-1.4pt from the last wrapped line of a gloss) and B7 (sub-point
% alignment noise across the five bands' left-column baselines);
% justified, not fixed.
\begin{figure}[H]
\centering
\pdfigurehue{pdcobalt}%

  \def\w{11.2}  \def\h{2.15}

    4/{pins}/{$H(\text{data})$, $H(\text{agent})$, $H(\text{runtime})$, $H(\text{policy})$}/{four hashes -- each pins an attested measurement, not the live thing}/{pd focus fill},
    3/{permissions}/{function, tools}/{fixes what may run and what it may call}/{pd neutral fill},
    2/{recipients}/{recipients, output schemas}/{fixes who may receive a result, and in what shape}/{pd neutral fill},
    1/{bounds}/{budgets, retention}/{bounds output bits, queries, and time; retention fixes key destruction}/{pd neutral fill},
    0/{remedies}/{validators, payment, liability}/{validators name the success evidence and dispute procedure; payment and liability are the guarantee}/{pd neutral fill}}{
      \draw[\s] (0,{\i*\h}) rectangle (\w,{\i*\h+\h});
      \node[pd title,anchor=north west,text width=2.3cm] at (0.22,{\i*\h+\h-0.18}) {\name};
      \node[pd label,anchor=north west,text width=3.55cm,align=left]
        at (2.75,{\i*\h+\h-0.18}) {\fields};
      \node[pd label,text=pdinkmuted,anchor=north west,text width=4.55cm,align=left]

  \node[pd kind] at (1.35,{5*\h+0.35}) {role};
  \node[pd kind] at (4.5,{5*\h+0.35}) {fields};
  \node[pd kind] at (8.8,{5*\h+0.35}) {what it fixes};
  \node[pd note,anchor=north west,align=left,text width=10.9cm]
    at (0.22,-0.42) {any change to any field makes a new hash for $C$ and requires both Derek's and Erin's signatures again};
\end{tikzpicture}
\caption{The work order binds measurements, permitted execution, recipients, limits, and remedies. Hashes identify attested measurements, not live query-time state. Any field change requires both principals to sign again. [internal]}

\begin{table}[H]\centering\footnotesize
\caption{Complete mediation is the assumption that both enforceability and
conservation name explicitly.}
\label{sealed:tab:sealed-side-invariants}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{2.6cm} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.6cm}@{}}
\toprule
Invariant & States & Depended on by \\
\midrule
Label monotonicity & no label weakens without a declassification witness & every gate of Sec.~\ref{sealed:sec:sealed-design}; assumed silently by noninterference (Sec.~\ref{sealed:sec:sealed-noninterference}) \\
\textbf{Complete mediation} & every release has exactly one gate decision & \textbf{named explicitly}: the deployment assumption Enforceability (Sec.~\ref{sealed:sec:sealed-enforceability}) and Conservation (Sec.~\ref{sealed:sec:sealed-conservation}) both inherit \\
Provenance closure & every release traces to committed input, model, runtime, policy, and declassifier nodes & the receipt $R=\mathrm{Sign}(\ldots)$ of Sec.~\ref{sealed:sec:sealed-design} \\
Replay safety & each job nonce settles at most once & the receipt's nonce field and the dual-attested key release's fresh nonce (Sec.~\ref{sealed:sec:sealed-design}, Fig.~\ref{sealed:fig:sealed-dual-attestation}) \\
Measurement binding & neither secret key is released for a different runtime or policy & the dual-attested key release ceremony directly (Fig.~\ref{sealed:fig:sealed-dual-attestation}) \\
Rollback detectability & accepted epochs strictly increase in both external ledgers & the $\varepsilon$-ledger's append-only journal (Sec.~\ref{sealed:sec:sealed-conservation}) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

\begin{table}[H]\centering\footnotesize
\caption{Six things this design does not promise, why not, and where the
residual is priced. A contract that implies any of these overclaims.}
\label{sealed:tab:sealed-not-promised}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.5cm} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{3.3cm}@{}}
\toprule
Not promised & Why not & Residual priced by \\
\midrule
Zero model leakage under unlimited adaptive queries to Derek & Derek \emph{intentionally observes} evaluations of $M$; unlimited black-box access enables model extraction & out of model: bounded only by the contracted query-and-output interface \\
Zero data leakage with arbitrary natural-language telemetry to Erin & that channel is exactly the $q\cdot b$ budget; ``zero'' needs $b=0$ & the $q\cdot b$ budget (Sec.~\ref{sealed:sec:sealed-budget}) \\
Elimination of timing, cache, speculative, firmware, or physical channels & the noninterference guarantee is possibilistic & out of model; padded and scheduled, not closed \\
Confidentiality through an unapproved external model or tool provider & a remote API that reads plaintext is another trusted reader & not priced: the model must run inside the confidential domain, or the guarantee does not apply \\
Correctness of the answer & the receipt proves what the measured system reported, not that it is true & out of model \\
Literal deletion of information already observed, availability under refusal, or collusion resistance & each needs a strictly stronger threat model & needs MPC or homomorphic backends, not priced here \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

source.excerpt:
\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.20\textwidth}p{0.34\textwidth}p{0.38\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{State-of-nature failure} & \textbf{Concrete form in a coding swarm} & \textbf{The primitive that answers it} \\
\midrule
Resource conflict & Two agents edit the same file/region; one silently clobbers the other &
A \textbf{claim} --- an advisory announcement that an agent intends to touch a
file or region --- backed by a database uniqueness constraint that makes a
double-claim physically impossible. \\
Illegibility & A pull request or session whose intent and effect a human cannot read in bounded time &
A \textbf{digest-with-zoom} surface (\S\ref{ls:sec:zoom}): a summary that is a lens onto
the underlying artifact, never a replacement for it. \\
Lies / confident-wrong & An agent reports completion (``all green'') without having verified &
An \textbf{honest-attestation} discipline: a self-report that distinguishes
\emph{verified-good} from \emph{no-evidence-of-bad} and refuses to claim what it
cannot check --- ``a green that wasn't checked is a lie.'' \\
Footguns & Irreversible action (force-push, delete) on a stale or wrong premise &
Footgun guards (\S\ref{ls:sec:landing}); the open problem this chapter frames is
replacing hand-maintained rule corpora with a structural authority. \\
Illegible authority & The coordinator blocks an agent and the operator cannot see \emph{why} &
The \emph{legible-sovereign rule} (\S\ref{ls:sec:authority}): every act of authority is
a logged, named, zoomable event. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{The state-of-nature failure taxonomy, the concrete coding-swarm form of
each, and the class of primitive that answers it. The fifth row --- \emph{illegible
authority} --- is the one Hobbes himself got wrong for software, and it is the crux
of this chapter (\S\ref{ls:sec:authority}).}
\label{ls:tab:taxonomy}
\end{table}

% Brief (tikz-diagram-craft), register row ch4-33.
% Reader question: given a flagged set that still contains a few true
%   positives, how many fewer opens does adaptive group-testing need than
%   reading every flag, and at what density does that stop paying?
% Claim: the guaranteed advantage adv(d)=1/(d(2*ceil(log2(1/d))+4)) crosses
%   1 at flagged-set density d=1/12: below that density zoom guarantees a
%   win, above it flat inspection can no longer be beaten on the worst case.
% Evidence: adv(1/12)=1.00 (crossing); adv(10/2500)=12.5, the F=2500,k=10
%   configuration whose realized mean was 162.6 opens (15.3x, better than
%   the 12.5x guarantee); adv(32/4096)=7.11 at the F=4096,k=32 tightness
%   config, where the exact tight formula lands on 511 queries, measured
%   511 exactly [internal, zoom_bound_check.py, run this pass].
% Must distinguish: the crossing point (adv=1, breakeven) from the two
%   worked configurations; that adv(d) is a genuine step function (the
%   ceiling), not a smooth curve, so no interpolation is drawn between
%   its jumps.
% Grammar chosen: threshold/regime plot, log-x density against guaranteed
%   advantage, a step curve (const plot) with a breakeven guide at adv=1.
% Grammar rejected: a bar chart of adv at the two named (F,k) configurations
%   would state the two numbers but hide the crossing itself -- the
%   chapter's point that d<=1/12 is a real, continuous threshold, not a
%   property of the two worked examples alone.
% Five-second test: "at the chapter's own F=2500,k=10 point, is the density
%   left or right of the d=1/12 crossing, and by how much?"
\begin{figure}[H]
\centering
\pdfigurehue{pdteal}%
\begin{tikzpicture}[pd figure]
\begin{axis}[pd axis,
  width=7.8cm,height=5.2cm,
  xmode=log,
  xmin=0.002,xmax=0.4,ymin=0,ymax=23,
  xtick={0.002,0.004,0.00781,0.0833,0.4},
  xticklabels={0.002,0.004,1/128,1/12,0.4},
  ytick={0,5,10,20},
  xlabel={flagged-set density $d=k/F$ (log scale)},
  ylabel={guaranteed advantage $\mathrm{adv}(d)$},
  clip=false,axis on top]
  \addplot[pd warn series,line width=.9pt,domain=0.002:0.4,samples=2] {1};
  \node[pd label,anchor=south east] at (axis cs:0.4,1) {breakeven: adv $=1$};
  \addplot[pd focus rule,line width=1.05pt,const plot,domain=0.002:0.4,samples=140,smooth=false]
    {1/(x*(2*ceil(ln(1/x)/ln(2))+4))};
  \draw[pd guide] (axis cs:0.0833,0) -- (axis cs:0.0833,1);
  \node[pd focus datum] at (axis cs:0.0833,1) {};
  \node[pd focus label,anchor=south west] at (axis cs:0.10,4.5) {$d{=}1/12$};
  \node[pd datum] at (axis cs:0.004,12.5) {};
  \node[pd label,anchor=south west,text width=2.8cm,align=left] at (axis cs:0.0043,14.0)
    {$F{=}2500,k{=}10$: $12.5\times$};
  \node[pd datum] at (axis cs:0.00781,7.11) {};
  \node[pd label,anchor=north west,text width=2.5cm,align=left] at (axis cs:0.011,6.0)
    {$F{=}4096,k{=}32$: $7.1\times$};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
\caption{Adaptive halving guarantees an advantage when $d<1/12$. At $F=2500,k=10$, its guarantee is $12.5\times$; the harness mean is $15.3\times$, distinct from that worst-case bound. [internal, \protect\path{zoom_bound_check.py}]}
\label{fig:zoom-advantage}
\end{figure}

\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\caption{These objectives act on different objects. The incompatibility theorems compare the commensurable pairs: rows 1--2 rank the same items; rows 2--3 score the same trace. [internal]}
\label{ls:tab:ls-three-losses}
\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}p{0.155\textwidth} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.19\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Loss} & \textbf{Input space / what is optimized over} & \textbf{Objective and loss metric} & \textbf{Target consumer} \\
\midrule
Directory candidate fit \newline (\S\ref{ls:sec:relevance})
& a (candidate, query) pair $(c,q)$; optimized over the live candidate set
& \emph{Maximize} $\mathrm{fit}(c,q)=\mathrm{clamp}(z(c,q),0,1)$,
Eq.~\ref{ls:eq:fit}. Wrongness is measured in \emph{mis-routing}: a capable
candidate ranked below an incapable one
& the routing agent, choosing who to ask \\
Human oversight regret \newline (\S\ref{ls:sec:sdt}, \S\ref{ls:sec:tokens-digest})
& a compaction $D$ of a trace $E$; optimized over what to surface under budget
& \emph{Minimize} $L_{\mathrm{op}}(D)=\sum_{e\in E\setminus D}\mathrm{regret}(e)$
with $\mathrm{regret}=\mathrm{stakes}\times\mathrm{irrev}\times\mathrm{anomaly}$
(Eq.~\ref{ls:eq:regret}). Wrongness is measured in \emph{unreviewed
irreversible loss}
& the human operator, deciding whether to intervene \\
Successor continuation \newline (\S\ref{ls:sec:tokens-digest})
& a compaction $D$ of the same trace $E$
& \emph{Minimize}
$L_{\mathrm{succ}}(D)=\mathrm{KL}\bigl(P_{\mathrm{next}}(\cdot\mid E)\,\|\,P_{\mathrm{next}}(\cdot\mid D)\bigr)$.
Wrongness is measured in \emph{bits of predictive divergence} about the next
action
& the successor agent, resuming the task \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.25}
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.14\textwidth}p{0.46\textwidth}p{0.32\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Signal} & \textbf{What it measures} & \textbf{Push or pull} \\
\midrule
$\mathrm{file}$  & Recent claims on the files named in the query & \emph{Pull} --- the claim record, not a self-report \\
$\mathrm{note}$  & Text similarity over the candidate's written notes & \emph{Pull} --- written for another purpose \\
$\mathrm{epis}$  & Text similarity over past episodes the candidate closed & \emph{Pull} --- outcomes, already witnessed \\
$\mathrm{ident}$ & Declared role and identity of the candidate & \emph{Push} --- asserted, cheap to inflate \\
$\mathrm{skill}$ & Declared/embedded capability, nearest-neighbor in the skill index & \emph{Push} --- asserted, and stale by default \\
$\mathrm{load}$  & How busy the candidate already is (penalty, $-w_\ell$) & \emph{Pull} --- observed occupancy \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.20\textwidth}p{0.22\textwidth}p{0.18\textwidth}p{0.28\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Strategy} & \textbf{What it drops} & \textbf{Failure if abused} & \textbf{When it is the right tool} \\
\midrule
Recursive summary & Older prose, re-summarized & Confident fabrication (rung 3) & Never as the \emph{only} record; only over durable artifacts re-read each round \\
Edge-placement & Nothing; reorders & --- & Whenever a fact is critical: put it first or last (counters lost-in-the-middle) \\
External note-taking & In-context detail, kept on disk & Notes nobody reads & Decisions and rationale that a successor must recover \\
Sub-agent isolation & Child context the parent never sees & Parent loses zoomability into the child & Bounded sub-tasks whose only output the parent needs is a result \\
Decay / forgetting & Stale coordination traces, continuously & Live signal aged out too fast & Ephemeral coordination state (claims, presence), where staleness is the enemy \\
Eviction + pointer & The artifact body; keep an address & Dangling pointer if the artifact moves & Reconstructable artifacts (a diff, a log) addressable on demand \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Six compaction strategies. Preserve access to critical artifacts
(Thm.~\ref{ls:thm:lowerbound}); rebuild summaries from durable sources, not
earlier summaries.}
\label{ls:tab:compaction}
\end{table}

% Brief (tikz-diagram-craft), breaking the sec:hayek desert (no register
% row; assignment names 4.9.3 as a no-visual run to break).
% Reader question: are the political-theory warning (Scott) and the
%   economics warning (Hayek) two separate cautions, or one claim reached
%   from two poles?
% Claim: Scotts legibility-destroys-metis warning and Hayeks dispersed,
%   non-aggregable knowledge argument converge on one shared claim -- the
%   binding constraint is decentralized, non-spawnable knowledge held in
%   one head -- and Scotts own constructive sequel supplies the one
%   prescription: preserve the spaces where metis lives.
% Evidence: sec:hayek, whitepaper/legible-swarm.tex (Hayek 1945, Scott
%   1998, Scott 2012), this pass.
% Must distinguish: the two independent source arguments from the one
%   claim they converge on; the claim from the prescription that follows
%   it, which is a distinct, later, constructive move.
% Grammar chosen: provenance/convergence chain, two named sources into one
%   claim into one prescription, since the point is literally that two
%   argument threads land on the same conclusion.
% Grammar rejected: a two-column comparison table (Scott vs Hayek) would
%   state each argument's content but hide the convergence itself, which
%   is the sentence's whole claim ("the same warning at two scales" /
%   "the other half of Scotts argument from the opposite pole").
% Five-second test: do the two named sources support different claims, or
%   the same one?
\begin{figure}[H]
\centering
\pdfigurehue{pdteal}%
\begin{tikzpicture}[pd figure,x=1cm,y=1cm]
  \node[pd state,minimum width=3.9cm,text width=3.5cm,align=center] (S)
    at (2.30,4.50) {Scott 1998: legibility flattens the metis that made the system work};
  \node[pd state,minimum width=3.9cm,text width=3.5cm,align=center] (H)
    at (7.10,4.50) {Hayek 1945: knowledge is dispersed, particular, non-aggregable};
  \node[pd focus state,minimum width=7.0cm,text width=6.4cm,align=center] (C)
    at (4.70,2.30) {the binding constraint is decentralized, non-spawnable knowledge held in one head};
  \node[pd ready state,minimum width=7.0cm,text width=6.4cm,align=center] (P)
    at (4.70,0.30) {Scott 2012: preserve the spaces where metis lives; do not flatten them};
  \draw[pd focus arrow] (S) -- (C);
  \draw[pd focus arrow] (H) -- (C);
  \draw[pd ready arrow] (C) -- (P);
\end{tikzpicture}
\caption{Scott and Hayek offer complementary cautions: administrative legibility can erase local knowledge. Scott's later work suggests preserving the spaces where practical knowledge develops. [interpretive synthesis]}
\label{fig:hayek-scott}
\end{figure}

Implementation and status
The body of this chapter argues mechanisms on their merits and
does not depend on any of them being built.
This appendix —
and only this appendix — records the concrete engineering status
of each mechanism in the reference implementation, named Port
Daddy. We use four honest labels, with one rule for the whole ta‑
ble: confusing what is implemented with what is merely specified
is itself the failure the paper argues against, so each row carries its
evidence.
implemented = code exists in the reference implementation today;
partial = code exists but is partial, unwired, or honest about a known
gap; specified = a concrete, accepted design with no merged imple‑
mentation; proposed = a mechanism argued in this chapter with no
design document yet.
A second key, in the same grammar, labels claims rather than code.
Every formal result in this chapter carries exactly one of these mark‑
ers directly under it, and the paper carries no free‑text status notes
outside them: verified = independently re‑derived and checked nu‑
merically, or subjected to a pre‑registered falsification sweep, out‑
side this document; proved here = argued here with a proof or proof
sketch and not independently checked; unproved = stated as a de‑
sign target whose proof is not carried in this chapter. The two keys
are orthogonal on purpose — a verified result about a proposed
mechanism is a perfectly ordinary state of affairs, and conflating
them is the failure this appendix exists to prevent.

Chapter 5. From Spawn to Person
analogue of an over‑grazed pasture. Ostrom’s finding on durable
common‑pool institutions is the relevant prior art here, and it argues
against both of the framings this section rejects: not open access (a
window each agent sets for itself), and not an imposed global con‑
stant (“∞, forever, for everyone”), but a window set by the partici‑
pants with clear boundaries, graduated sanctions, and cheap local
conflict resolution — which is a fair description of what a harbor’s
tombstone‑plus‑window policy actually has to be.
“Reputation never ends” as a virtue is wrong twice over: it makes
a fraudulent outcome permanent (needs the tombstone of Prop‑
erty 5.12.1), and it asserts ∞‑memory is optimal when the reputation‑
bubble literature shows it usually is not. Engage bounded memory
as a parameter; do not assert no‑decay as a feature.
Two corrections to the cheerful framing: (1) reputation is mono‑
tone in honest outcomes but individually revocable via a propagat‑
ing tombstone — a saga compensation, not in‑place mutation; (2)
bounded memory is a design parameter (Liu–Skrzypacz reputation
bubbles), not an anti‑feature to assert away.
5.13
What this chapter hands the market
This chapter is the bridge; its output is a precise hand‑off to The Har‑
bor Economy. We summarize what is delivered, what is borrowed,
and what is explicitly owed.

\toprule

\midrule
\endhead
\midrule
\endfoot
\bottomrule

Episodic memory (Subsystem 1) & \BUILT &
Durable typed episodes promoted from execution history; runs in production. \\
Restart subsystem (Subsystem 2) & \BUILTWEAK &
Heartbeat-staleness detector that salvages dead agents; forwards a \emph{summary}, not execution state. \\
Outcome ledger (Subsystem 3) & \BUILTWEAK &
Durable commitments, daemon-derived deadlines, oracle-bound closure, API/CLI, and overdue detection ship; neutral grading, sanctions, and reputation binding do not. \\
Cost meter (efficiency axis) & \BUILT &
Per-task token/wall-clock/dollar accounting recorded today. \\
Local non-forgeable identity & \BUILTWEAK &
Daemon-minted actor-soul, lookup credential, and bounded newcomer pool ship; full write-boundary enforcement and legacy migration do not. \\
Capability jail (capability $\ne$ permission) & \DESIGNED &
Per-agent tool-allowlist and scoped filesystem; specified. \\
Honest-attestation discipline & \BUILT &
``Report all-good only when verified'' is an enforced engineering rule. \\
Multi-dimensional reputation & \shortstack[l]{\DESIGNED\\[-1pt]to \VISION} &
No reputation component yet; the substrate it scores over is partly built. \\
Neutral-judge ceremony (Proto.~\ref{stp:proto:judge}) & \shortstack[l]{\DESIGNED\\[-1pt]to \VISION} &
Bonding and task-planning primitives exist; the hiring ceremony is designed. \\
Skill-helpfulness schema (Proto.~\ref{stp:proto:skill}) & \DESIGNED &
Skill grafting is observable; the witnessed-event schema is specified. \\
Tombstone revocation (Proto.~\ref{stp:proto:tombstone}) & \DESIGNED &
Append-only ledger semantics are designed; cross-harbor propagation is \VISION. \\
Cross-operator attestation & \VISION &
The unbuilt keystone for the market; owed to \pdchapref{he}{The Harbor Economy}. \\
\end{xltabular}

Chapter Appendices
5.A
Implementation status of the refer‑
ence system
The body of this chapter is written to stand on its own: every mecha‑
nism is described as a component (a memory record, a checkpoint
subsystem, a witnessed‑outcome ledger) and graded on the neu‑
tral maturity scale (implemented / partial / specified / proposed).
This appendix grounds that scale in a concrete reference system
— a running coordination daemon for local agent swarms — so a
reader who wants to know “which of these actually runs today” can
check. Nothing in the body depends on this appendix; it exists so
the maturity labels are falsifiable rather than rhetorical.

% Figure IV.new --- the Myerson-Satterthwaite wedge: efficient trades the
% mechanism itself refuses. ch6-15 (register: must) and ADDENDUM 4 (breaks
% the visual-less run at sec:ms).
%
% Reader question: how much real, mutually-beneficial trade does budget
% balance and incentive compatibility actually cost the market?
% Claim: on the chapter's own (v,c) square, the double auction refuses a
% 10-cr efficient trade at the worked point (Bob v=70, Alice c=60) because
% v-c=10<M/4=22.5; integrated over the whole square, that wedge is
% 7/32 (approx 21.9%) of all draws, independent of M.
% Evidence: Thm. ms (Myerson-Satterthwaite); Chatterjee-Samuelson linear
% equilibrium, trade iff v-c>=M/4; worked point (70,60); wedge probability
% a(2M-a)/(2M^2) at a=M/4 = 7/32.
% Must distinguish: the "trade happens" corner (v-c>=M/4) from the
% "efficient but refused" wedge (0<=v-c<M/4, real surplus left on the
% table) from the genuinely-no-surplus region (v<c).
% Grammar chosen: regime plot in (v,c) space, the wedge filled between two
% lines (S11 fillbetween), the worked point dropped to both axes (atlas
% first choice). Grammar rejected: the probability alone in prose (already
% stated) -- it hides that the wedge is a fixed-width band running the
% whole diagonal, not a corner case.
% Five-second test: a reader can find (70,60) inside the shaded wedge and
% see it sits on the trade side of the diagonal but the wrong side of the
% refusal line.
\begin{figure}[H]
\centering
\pdfigurehue{pdgold}%
\begin{tikzpicture}[pd figure]
\begin{axis}[pd axis,
  width=8.3cm,height=7.2cm,
  xmin=0,xmax=90,ymin=0,ymax=90,
  xtick={0,30,70,90},ytick={0,30,60,90},
  xlabel={Bob's value $v$ (cr)},
  ylabel={Alice's cost $c$ (cr)}]
  % Explicit clipped band: only 0 < v-c < 22.5 is efficient but refused.
  % No stroked polygon edge may create a fictitious decision boundary.
  \path[fill=pdamber!18,draw=none]
    (axis cs:0,0) -- (axis cs:90,90) -- (axis cs:90,67.5)
    -- (axis cs:22.5,0) -- cycle;
  \addplot[pd guide,mark=none,domain=0:90,samples=2] {x};
  \addplot[pd value series,mark=none,domain=22.5:90,samples=2] {x-22.5};
  \node[pd label,anchor=west,align=left] at (axis cs:7,79)
    {no positive surplus\\$v<c$};
  \node[pd value label,align=left] at (axis cs:53,12)
    {trade\\$v-c\ge22.5$};
  \node[pd label,anchor=west,align=left] at (axis cs:3,45)
    {efficient, refused\\$7/32$ of all draws};
  \draw[pd rule,line width=.5pt] (axis cs:29,37) -- (axis cs:38,28);
  \draw[pd guide] (axis cs:70,0) -- (axis cs:70,60) -- (axis cs:0,60);
  \node[pd datum] at (axis cs:70,60) {};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
\caption{Independent uniform values and costs on $[0,90]$\,cr are an
illustrative prior, not market data. The marked rental offers $10$\,cr of
surplus, below this equilibrium's $22.5$\,cr trade threshold.}
\label{fig:he-ms-wedge}
\end{figure}

\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\small
\caption{Which promise each gap threatens. The two gaps that reach the
\emph{conservation} invariant are the urgent ones, because conservation is the only
claim in this chapter graded \Built{} --- a hole there falsifies something that is
currently true, rather than deferring something that is not yet true.}
\label{he:tab:gaps}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.32\textwidth} l >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Gap} & \textbf{Threatens} & \textbf{How it bites} \\
\midrule
Operator exit / harbor death & conservation &
  orphaned escrow rows have no settlement path, so
  $\text{wallet}+\text{escrow}+\text{commons}$ stops summing to supply \\
Float-plan amendment under scope drift & conservation &
  a mid-flight re-spec moves value with no matching debit unless the top-up/refund
  delta is escrowed \\
Cross-boundary key rotation & cross-boundary safety &
  a delegation already held by $B$ may verify against a key $A$ has retired \\
Skill versioning & Sybil-resistance &
  a v2 content hash is a fresh identity, so the lemons problem and the
  whitewash both reappear at every version bump \\
Multi-dimensional reputation aggregation & incentive compatibility &
  an unspecified aggregation rule is an unspecified target, and any fixed scalar
  collapse re-creates a Goodhart objective \\
Incentive-compatible arbitration capacity & incentive compatibility &
  Fix~B (\S\ref{he:sec:ic}) prices one judge; it does not price a judge pool under
  load, where rubber-stamping is the cheap strategy \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\small
\caption{How the harbor economy sits relative to the nearest prior art on each axis.}
\label{he:tab:related}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{2.4cm} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Axis} & \textbf{Nearest prior art} & \textbf{What the harbor does differently} \\
\midrule
Market structure & Two-sided platforms~\pdcite{mega176} &
  Three incentive constraints (labor / capital / IP) on one escrow object \\
Settlement across distrust & Atomic swaps~\pdcite{mega207};
  cross-chain deals~\pdcite{mega208} &
  Bounded (not trustless) escrow for \emph{non-fungible, reputation-priced} bonds \\
Revocation & PKI revocation lists; Certificate Transparency~\pdcite{mega204} &
  Gossip-converged filters with a priced, named attacker window \\
Reputation revocation & Sagas compensation~\pdcite{mega209} &
  Tombstone propagation --- no conserved quantity to compensate \\
Grading / IC signal & Folk theorems~\pdcite{mega201} &
  Strategy-proof machine-checkable oracle \emph{or} contractual adjudication with modeled judge incentives \\
Agent transaction rails & UCP~\pdcite{mega213}; ACP~\pdcite{mega215};
  AP2 mandates~\pdcite{mega214} &
  They standardize the transaction and name trust out of scope; the harbor prices
  and enforces the trust layer they delegate away \\
Purchased assurance & Delegated computation~\pdcite{mega217}; AI-safety
  debate~\pdcite{mega218} &
  Prices assurance as $k$ independently bonded test-writers under a Becker-style
  re-audit rate, against a mutation-testing oracle \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

\begin{figure}[H]

\SGMeasuredFigure{he-assurance}{%
\begin{tikzpicture}[pd figure]
  % The upper and lower axes share the same reviewer-count domain. This is an
  % aligned comparison, not one curve with two incompatible y scales.
  \begin{axis}[
    pd evidence axis,
    width=263pt,height=126pt,
    xmin=.8,xmax=6.25,
    xtick={1,2,3,4,5,6},xticklabels=\empty,
    ymode=log,log basis y=10,
    ymin=.3,ymax=60,
    ytick={1,10,40},yticklabels={1\%,10\%,40\%},
    ylabel={conditional miss probability (log scale)},
    clip=false,
  ]
    % Compact assumption rail: no formula/caption duplication, but d's meaning
    % remains visible in plain language.
    \node[pd label,anchor=south west,inner sep=0pt,yshift=13pt,
      text width=263pt,align=left]
      at (rel axis cs:0,1.24)
      {$d=.6$: a reviewer finds and reports a given flaw};

    % Series labels live in a reserved band above the data, with leaders to
    % exact curve points. They do not sit on the dashed comparator or decay.
    \node[pd label,text=pdteal,anchor=south west,inner sep=0pt]
      at (rel axis cs:0.02,1.08) {independent draws};
    \node[pd label,anchor=south west,inner sep=0pt]
      at (rel axis cs:0.60,1.08) {one shared error};
    \draw[pd guide]
      (axis cs:2,16) -- (rel axis cs:0.16,1.02);
    \draw[pd guide]
      (axis cs:4.4,40) -- (rel axis cs:0.68,1.02);

    % The 1% line is a decision reference from the worked example.
    \draw[draw=pdinkmuted,densely dashed,line width=.7pt]
      (axis cs:.8,1) -- (axis cs:6.25,1);
    \node[pd label,anchor=east,inner sep=0pt,xshift=-3pt]
      at (axis cs:6.22,1.7) {1\% target};

    % Risk: independent reviewers decay geometrically; a perfectly shared
    % outcome has one effective draw and therefore remains at 1-d=.4.
    \addplot[pd legible series,domain=1:6,samples=6]
      {100*(1-.6)^x};
    \addplot[pd evidence comparison,domain=1:6,samples=6]
      {40};
  \end{axis}

  \begin{axis}[
    pd evidence axis,
    anchor=south west,at={(0pt,-96pt)},
    width=263pt,height=70pt,
    xmin=.8,xmax=6.25,
    xtick={1,2,3,4,5,6},
    ymin=0,ymax=6.5,
    ytick={0,1,2,3,4,5,6},
    ylabel={budget units},
    xlabel={reviewer count $k$},
    clip=false,
  ]
    % C_k=k*(b+c_B), normalized so the unknown bond carry is not fabricated.

  \node[pd label,anchor=center,inner sep=0pt,text width=263pt,align=center]
    at (131.5pt,-13pt)
    {One budget unit: bounty $b$ + bond carry $c_B$};
\end{tikzpicture}
}

% Brief (tikz-diagram-craft). Register row ch7-11 (should).
% Reader question: how do the three isolation tiers order, and what does
%   each buy or cost?
% Claim: the three tiers strictly order by strength (I0 subset I1 subset
%   I2); I1 is the default; choosing I1 vs I2 is an economics decision
%   (Section 5), not a security one.
% Evidence: website-v2/public/whitepaper/agent-transactions-whitepaper.tex
%   Definition (Isolation Levels), sec:isolation: I0 none (shared working
%   directory, no conflict detection, maximum parallelism, no safety); I1
%   advisory (shared directory, file claims registered, conflicts detected
%   and reported but not enforced -- the default); I2 structural (separate
%   git worktrees, filesystem-level isolation, conflicts deferred to
%   sequential merge).
% Must distinguish: the strict ordering by strength from what each rung
%   adds relative to the one below; I1 as the default from I0/I2 as
%   deliberate choices; the I1-vs-I2 choice as economic, forward-pointing
%   to Section 5's Sen-grounded argument.
% Grammar chosen: three-rung ordered ladder (Hasse-style containment), each
%   rung naming what it adds and its cost, weakest at the bottom. Rejected:
%   a plain enumerated list, which the chapter already gives in prose and
%   would not show the strict-subset ordering the definition states.
% Five-second test: a reader reads bottom-to-top as "less safety, more
%   parallelism" and top-to-bottom as the reverse, with I1 marked default.
\begin{figure}[H]
\centering
\pdfigurehue{pdgold}%
\begin{tikzpicture}[pd figure,x=1cm,y=1cm]
  \def\ldy{3.35}  % rung pitch: prose height plus a visible transition shaft
  \def\ldw{7.6}   % rung width
  \tikzset{rung/.style={pd label,minimum width=\ldw cm,minimum height=2.3cm,
    draw,line width=.9pt,align=left,text width=6.9cm,inner xsep=8pt,inner ysep=8pt}}

% Brief (tikz-diagram-craft).
% Reader question: does the competitive-insurance mechanism Pareto-dominate
%   the static baseline, and what breaks that dominance?
% Claim: with no cartel, dominance holds in at least 86% of trials across
%   reputation noise and insurer count; a three-insurer cartel collapses
%   dominance below the 50% criterion once noise passes sigma_r = 0.3.
% Evidence: proofs/bonded/pareto/simulation.mjs, simulation.run.log
%   (trials_per_config=2000, 50 transactions/trial), pareto_dominance_rate
%   at n_insurers=5 across cartelSize in {0,1,3} and sigma_r in
%   {0,.1,.3,.5}; and at sigma_r=0, cartelSize=0 across n_insurers in
%   {3,5,10} [verified, simulation.mjs].
% Must distinguish: the no-cartel baseline from the one- and three-colluder
%   regimes, and where each series crosses the 50% dominance criterion.
% Grammar chosen: two aligned pgfplots panels sharing the dominance-rate
%   axis, direct-labelled series, Monte Carlo import from the committed
%   script. Rejected: a single combined panel varying both sigma_r and n at
%   once, because the two parameters would be confounded in one curve.
% Five-second test: a reader says the three-colluder cartel is the only
%   series that falls below the 50% line, and names where it does.
\begin{figure}[H]
\centering
\pdfigurehue{pdgold}%
\begin{tikzpicture}[pd figure]
\begin{groupplot}[
  group style={group size=2 by 1, horizontal sep=1.05cm},
  pd axis,width=4.3cm,height=4.05cm,
  ymin=0,ymax=1,ytick={0,.25,.5,.75,1},
  yticklabels={0,.25,.5,.75,1},
]
\nextgroupplot[
  xlabel={reputation noise $\sigma_r$},
  title={(a) vs noise, $n=5$},
  xtick={0,.1,.3,.5},
]
  \addplot[pd warn series,line width=.7pt,domain=-.02:.52] {0.5};
  \addplot[pd ready series,mark=o] coordinates {(0,.861)(.1,.675)(.3,.006)(.5,.002)};
  \addplot[pd focus series,mark=square] coordinates {(0,.877)(.1,.916)(.3,.175)(.5,.075)};
  \addplot[pd breach series,mark=triangle] coordinates {(0,.926)(.1,.844)(.3,.208)(.5,.163)};
  \node[pd focus label,anchor=south west] at (axis cs:.28,.945) {1 colluder};
  \node[pd breach label,anchor=south west] at (axis cs:.02,.945) {3 colluders};
\nextgroupplot[
  xlabel={insurer count $n$},
  title={(b) vs $n$, no cartel},
  xtick={3,5,10},
]
  \addplot[pd warn series,line width=.7pt,domain=2.5:10.5] {0.5};
  \addplot[pd ready series,mark=o] coordinates {(3,.906)(5,.861)(10,.739)};
\end{groupplot}
\node[pd label,rotate=90,anchor=south] at (-0.95,2.15) {Pareto-dominance rate};
\end{tikzpicture}
\caption{Competition's advantage over the static baseline depends on noise,
collusion and insurer count: more insurers do not guarantee better outcomes.
2{,}000 trials per configuration, 50 transactions each; Wilson 95\% intervals
are within $\pm0.02$ of the plotted rates.
[verified, \protect\path{proofs/bonded/pareto/simulation.mjs}]}
\label{fig:pareto-mc-inline}
\end{figure}

%   the commons' own deficit is fully reimbursed once the deposit crosses
%   about 200 USD -- the coverage cap. Raising the deposit protects the
%   commons but never the deterrence claim.

%   reaches zero from the (much higher, in fact never-reached) deposit that

% Brief (tikz-diagram-craft).
% Reader question: which per-round detection probability / patience pairs
%   keep a bid-rigging cartel sustainable, and which collapse it?
% Claim: cartel sustainability is a narrow band -- at delta=0.95 the
%   closed-form threshold p_d*=0.0478 and the simulated grid first flips
%   from sustainable to collapsed at p_d=0.05, a near-exact match; higher
%   patience (larger delta) widens the sustainable band only slightly.
% Evidence: proofs/bonded/pareto/simulation-cartel.run.log
%   (trials_per_config=5000, rounds=200, cartel_size=3), the sustainable
%   column across the full 8x4 (p_d, delta) grid tested
%   [verified, simulation-cartel.mjs]; the closed-form boundary
%   p_d^star(delta) = (pi_c-(1-delta)pi_d) / (L+delta*pi_d) from
%   sec:youle:a6, evaluated at each tested delta with pi_c=5/3, pi_d=4.95,
%   L=25. A faithful redraw of
%   website-v2/public/whitepaper/figures/fig-cartel-folk-theorem.pdf (its
%   left panel; the right panel, simulated mean rounds to first detection,
%   is not reproduced here -- see note below).
% Must distinguish: sustainable (S, amber, cartel persists) from collapsed
%   (C, teal, cartel fails) cells; the closed-form p_d* value at each
%   tested delta from the simulated flip point.
% Grammar chosen: categorical grid matrix (S12-adjacent: a matched/flagged
%   grid, mirroring the atlas's own heatmap prescription for ch7-36's
%   threat-band sweep), each cell a concrete tested instance, with the
%   closed-form p_d* row set beneath as an aligned tabularx legend.
%   Rejected: a continuous pgfplots log-axis heatmap with an overlaid
%   analytical boundary curve, matching the matplotlib original pixel for
%   pixel -- the curve threads eight unevenly log-spaced categories that a
%   discrete grid already states exactly, and forcing continuous pgfplots
%   axes onto eight named categories would misrepresent them as measured
%   on a continuum the sweep does not interpolate between.
% Five-second test: a reader sees the S/C frontier step rightward by at
%   most one column as delta rises, and reads off p_d*(0.95)=0.048 beside
%   the row where the grid itself flips at p_d=0.05.

  \def\ccy{0}      % top row centre
  \def\cch{.92}    % row pitch
  \tikzset{cell/.style={pd label,minimum width=.98cm,minimum height=.75cm,
    draw,line width=.5pt}}
  % column headers: p_d
  \foreach \j/\pd in {0/0.01,1/0.03,2/0.05,3/0.10,4/0.15,5/0.20,6/0.30,7/0.50}
    {\node[pd title,anchor=south] at ({\ccx+\j*\ccw},{\ccy+.56}) {\pd};}
  \node[pd label,anchor=south] at ({\ccx+3.5*\ccw},1.02) {per-round detection probability $p_d$};
  % row headers: delta, top to bottom 0.99, 0.95, 0.90, 0.80
  \foreach \i/\dl in {0/0.99,1/0.95,2/0.90,3/0.80}
    {\node[pd title,anchor=east] at ({\ccx-.70},{\ccy-\i*\cch}) {\dl};}
  \node[pd label,rotate=90,anchor=south] at (-1.42,{\ccy-1.5*\cch}) {discount factor $\delta$};
  % the tested grid: S = sustainable (amber), C = collapses (teal); every

source.excerpt:
\begin{lstlisting}[style=tlaplus, caption={TLA$^{+}$: Core Actions}]
Begin(a, escrow) ==
  /\ a \notin registered
  /\ escrow > 0    \* Must post collateral
  /\ registered' = registered \cup {a}
  /\ sessions' = [sessions EXCEPT ![a] =
       [status |-> "active", notes |-> <<>>,
        claims |-> {}, escrow |-> escrow]]
  /\ heartbeats' = [heartbeats EXCEPT ![a] = clock]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fileClaims, heldLocks,
                  salvageQueue, clock>>

ClaimFile(a, f) ==
  /\ a \in registered
  /\ sessions[a].status = "active"
  \* Advisory: always succeeds, reports conflicts
  /\ fileClaims' = [fileClaims EXCEPT ![f] =
       fileClaims[f] \cup {a}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<registered, sessions, heldLocks,
                  salvageQueue, heartbeats, clock>>

Commit(a) ==
  /\ a \in registered
  /\ sessions[a].status = "active"
  /\ sessions' = [sessions EXCEPT ![a] =
       [sessions[a] EXCEPT !.status = "settled",
                           !.escrow = 0]]
  \* Release all claims and locks
  /\ fileClaims' = [f \in Files |->
       fileClaims[f] \ {a}]
  /\ heldLocks' = [l \in Locks |->
       IF heldLocks[l] # NULL /\ heldLocks[l].owner = a
       THEN NULL ELSE heldLocks[l]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<registered, salvageQueue,
                  heartbeats, clock>>

Crash(a) ==
  /\ a \in registered
  /\ sessions[a].status = "active"
  /\ heartbeats' = [heartbeats EXCEPT ![a] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<registered, sessions, fileClaims,
                  heldLocks, salvageQueue, clock>>

Reap ==
  /\ \E a \in registered :
     /\ sessions[a].status = "active"
     /\ clock - heartbeats[a] >= DeadThreshold
     /\ sessions' = [sessions EXCEPT ![a] =
          [sessions[a] EXCEPT !.status = "abandoned"]]
     /\ salvageQueue' = salvageQueue \cup
          {[agent |-> a, status |-> "pending"]}
     /\ fileClaims' = [f \in Files |->
          fileClaims[f] \ {a}]
     /\ UNCHANGED <<registered, heldLocks,
                     heartbeats, clock>>

Salvage(successor, dead) ==
  /\ successor \in registered
  /\ sessions[successor].status = "active"
  /\ [agent |-> dead, status |-> "pending"]
       \in salvageQueue
  /\ salvageQueue' = (salvageQueue \
       {[agent |-> dead, status |-> "pending"]})
       \cup {[agent |-> dead,
              status |-> "resurrecting"]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<registered, sessions, fileClaims,
                  heldLocks, heartbeats, clock>>

Dismiss(dead) ==
  \* Irrecoverable information loss
  /\ [agent |-> dead, status |-> "pending"]
       \in salvageQueue
  /\ salvageQueue' = salvageQueue \
       {[agent |-> dead, status |-> "pending"]}
  /\ sessions' = [sessions EXCEPT ![dead] = NULL]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<registered, fileClaims, heldLocks,
                  heartbeats, clock>>

Tick == /\ clock' = clock + 1
        /\ UNCHANGED <<registered, sessions, fileClaims,
             heldLocks, salvageQueue, heartbeats>>
\end{lstlisting}

source.excerpt:
\begin{lstlisting}[style=tlaplus, caption={TLA$^{+}$: Safety and Liveness Properties}]
\* SAFETY: Every active session has positive escrow
EscrowInvariant ==
  \A a \in registered :
    sessions[a] # NULL /\ sessions[a].status = "active"
    => sessions[a].escrow > 0

\* SAFETY: Notes never shrink for active sessions
NoteMonotonicity ==
  \A a \in registered :
    sessions[a] # NULL /\ sessions[a].status = "active"
    => Len(sessions'[a].notes) >= Len(sessions[a].notes)

\* LIVENESS: Dead agents are eventually salvaged
\* or dismissed (under fairness)
CrashRecovery ==
  \A a \in Agents :
    [agent |-> a, status |-> "pending"] \in salvageQueue
    ~> [agent |-> a, status |-> "pending"]
         \notin salvageQueue

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(Reap) /\ WF_vars(Tick)

====
\end{lstlisting}

\textbf{Body of work} & \textbf{Borrowed} & \textbf{Departure} & \textbf{Why} \\
\midrule
Social contract theory & Authority accepted before interaction begins & The sovereign is a daemon whose rules are inspectable and whose consent is revocable per task & Agents can exit; Hobbes's subjects could not \\
Impossibility results & Liberalism against Pareto efficiency & Applied to enforced file claims & It is the reason claims stay advisory \\
Long-lived transactions & Compensation for work that outlives a transaction & Economic settlement in place of mechanical compensation & Compensation cannot undo an external effect; a bond can price it \\
BDI and generative agents & Beliefs, desires, intentions; memory streams & The evidence trail is read by an adversarial operator, not a private memory & The reader, not the agent, is the customer of the record \\
Capability-based security & Attenuable capabilities & Capabilities bind to bonded identities with settlement & Authority without liability is the failure the commons prices \\
Mechanism design & Incentive compatibility as the design target & Bonds priced by the claim-signaling threshold $\delta^{*}$, not by an optimal auction & The commons is a repeated game, not a one-shot sale \\
Agentic-commerce protocols & The credential envelope & The envelope carries authorization; the commons carries liability & A standard format shrinks the problem without settling it \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

% Table for ch8-06 -- the Witness-Log Admissibility properties (S2.3,
% prop:fh-witness), a classification (property x what it prevents) per the
% whitepaper figure system's own rule: a classification is a table, not a
% figure, mirroring Bonded's own Admissible KMS treatment.
%
% Reader question: what must the shared log guarantee for no harbor to
%   become sovereign over the others?
% Claim: five independent properties, each closing one specific failure;
%   dropping any one reopens a distinct way a harbor (or the log itself)
%   could become sovereign over the others.
% Evidence: prop:fh-witness's own five-item enumeration.
% Grammar rejected: a figure of the log as a chain of boxes would show
%   append-only alone; the other four properties are not structural, they
%   are guarantees about what the log lets an auditor conclude, which a
%   table's "prevents" column states directly.
% Five-second test: which property is the one that makes equivocation
%   provable, not just detectable?
\begin{table}[H]
\centering
\caption{Five witness-log properties, each closing a distinct federation
failure. [internal]}
\label{tab:fh-witness-log}
\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}l >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{property} & \textbf{what it prevents} \\
\midrule
append-only & retracting or reordering a published root after the fact \\
per-harbor latest-root binding & a harbor silently publishing two roots for one epoch \\
auditable consistency & an inconsistent history between two epochs going unverifiable \\
equivocation evidence & a proven contradiction requiring anything beyond the two signed roots \\
threshold publishability & publication itself requiring another daemon's permission \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}
